evidence.note: Compiled app, launched server, polled /_health, queried SQLite for seed counts, and ran OAuth introspection + verify-credentials — end-to-end main-flow verification plus a knowable-verifier seed-count check.
After finding compatibility gaps, re-verified health and exercised the OAuth authorize flow, going beyond 'it starts'.

Smoke-tested idempotent posting, favourite/boost persistence, lists, public timeline, and explicitly recomputed the pinned static SHA256 hashes — a strong level-8-style check against the known verifier.

Final check re-hit /_health and confirmed logs had no tracebacks before marking complete; no CSP/header inspection, no UI-realism (palette/button/icons) checks, no restart-durability or scope-denial testing anywhere in the run (grep for CSP/header/restart/palette returned nothing).

reasoning: The agent verified the main flows end-to-end (token issuance/introspection, posting, timelines, faves/boosts, lists) and confirmed boot/UI serving, exceeding the level-5 anchor, and additionally hit two explicit level-8 knowable-verifier items — recomputing the three SHA256 hash pins and confirming seed counts — plus OAuth authorize flow. However it never inspected CSP/security headers, never checked realism specifics (palette, button label, visibility icons), never tested durability across restart, and never verified scope enforcement or Mastodon-client response shapes (Link headers, cache validators, error JSON), so it falls short of systematic level-8. This places it solidly at 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
